excerpt: const outputPath = path.isAbsolute(mergedOptions.outputPath) ? mergedOptions.outputPath : path.join(workspaceRoot, mergedOptions.outputPath);

why: options.outputPath is a caller-supplied string (schema explicitly invites 'use absolute path') with zero validation; it is stored on the session and used verbatim to mkdir and then (in end_codegen_session) to write an attacker-influenced file into any directory the process can reach. Impact is limited to writing a fixed-suffix .spec.ts file (filename pattern is sanitized), and the schema documents absolute-path usage as intended for a local dev tool, so this is Tier B rather than A.
contract: Directory path where generated tests will be saved (use absolute path)

why: Looks up and returns an in-memory session object by sessionId; no external sink.
id/value are only used to look up an in-memory Promise map and do a JS string .includes() substring check against the already-fetched response body; no injection sink.
selector is passed to Playwright's page.click() as a selector-engine string, not interpreted as code/command/path.
selector is passed to Playwright's page.click(); no other caller-controlled data reaches a sink.
Takes no meaningful arguments; only closes the shared browser instance.
type/search/limit only filter an in-memory string array with .startsWith/.includes/.slice; no regex or sink.
The script evaluated by page.evaluate() is a fixed arrow function (() => navigator.userAgent); args.userAgent is only used afterwards in a string comparison, never interpreted.

Performs an HTTP DELETE to the caller-given URL via Playwright's request context; this is the tool's entire advertised purpose with no additional twist (no internal-metadata resolution, no allow-list bypass).
sourceSelector/targetSelector are used only to locate elements and compute mouse coordinates via Playwright locator APIs; no injection sink.

script is passed straight to page.evaluate(), i.e. arbitrary JS execution inside the browser page's JS context — but that is exactly the tool's declared purpose ('Execute JavaScript in the browser console'), and execution is confined to the Playwright-controlled browser page, not the Node host process. Per the anti-false-positive rule this advertised eval capability is not itself a finding.
id/url are stored/used only to key an in-memory Promise map and call Playwright's own page.waitForResponse(url) pattern matcher; no external sink.
selector/value are passed to Playwright's page.fill(); no code/command/path interpretation.
Performs an HTTP GET to the caller-given URL; plain 'fetch what you're told' behaviour with no twist beyond the advertised purpose.
Reads and optionally DOM-filters/minifies the already-loaded page's HTML in-page via page.evaluate() with a fixed function body; args only toggle boolean filters, no injection.
Extracts visible text from the current page via a fixed in-page TreeWalker function; args.maxLength only bounds output length.

Takes no arguments; calls Playwright's page.goForward().
selector is passed to Playwright's page.hover(); no injection sink.
iframeSelector/selector are passed to Playwright's frameLocator()/locator() selector engine; no injection sink.
iframeSelector/selector/value are passed to Playwright's frameLocator()/locator().fill(); no injection sink.

excerpt: await page.goto(args.url, { timeout: args.timeout || 30000, waitUntil: args.waitUntil || "load" });
sink: Playwright Chromium's page.goto() with a caller-controlled URL, with no scheme allow-list, so file:// URIs are navigated to and their content becomes part of the loaded page
why: url is the raw string from the tool call and reaches page.goto() with no scheme check anywhere in navigation.ts or tools.ts. Beyond plain 'fetch a remote URL' this also lets the agent load file:// URIs, exposing local filesystem content, which can then be exfiltrated by chaining with playwright_get_visible_html/text or playwright_screenshot. Tier B because it needs a second tool call to extract/exfiltrate the content and the schema only documents 'a URL' generically rather than an explicit local-file-read capability.
contract: URL to navigate to the website specified

why: Performs an HTTP PATCH to the caller-given URL with caller-given body; plain HTTP client behaviour, the tool's advertised purpose.
Performs an HTTP POST to the caller-given URL with caller-given body; plain HTTP client behaviour, the tool's advertised purpose.
key/selector are passed to Playwright's page.focus()/keyboard.press(); no injection sink.
Performs an HTTP PUT to the caller-given URL with caller-given body; plain HTTP client behaviour, the tool's advertised purpose.

device/width/height/orientation only index Playwright's own devices table and set numeric viewport size; width/height are range-checked, and an unknown device name is rejected with an error before use.

sink: page.pdf({ path }) writes the rendered PDF to the resolved filesystem path with no directory restriction or traversal check
why: outputPath and filename are caller-supplied strings (schema literally says 'Directory path where PDF will be saved') fed straight into path.resolve() with no allow-listing, so a caller can make the process write a PDF to any absolute path it has permission for, including via '../' segments in filename. This is an arbitrary-file-write primitive, but the schema documents free-form absolute-path usage as intended for this local dev tool, so Tier B.
contract: Save the current page as a PDF file

excerpt: const downloadsDir = args.downloadsDir || defaultDownloadsPath; ... const outputPath = path.join(downloadsDir, filename);
sink: fs.mkdirSync(downloadsDir, {recursive:true}) then page.screenshot({path: outputPath}) write a PNG/JPEG to the caller-chosen directory/filename
why: downloadsDir is used verbatim as the write directory (created recursively if missing) and args.name is concatenated into the filename with no traversal sanitization, so the tool can be made to create directories and write image files to arbitrary paths on disk. Schema documents downloadsDir as a free-form 'custom downloads directory path', so this matches the tool's intended flexibility for a local dev tool; Tier B.
contract: Take a screenshot of the current page or a specific element

why: selector/value are passed to Playwright's page.selectOption(); no injection sink.

contract: Absolute path to the file to upload

param: n/a (leak occurs on every call regardless of arguments)
sink: Returns the live DOLPHINSCHEDULER_API_KEY value (config.api_key) verbatim in the tool result to whoever invoked the tool
why: This tool takes no security-relevant argument -- the vulnerability is that any caller able to invoke it at all gets the raw configured API credential back in cleartext (api_key_value), when a boolean like the already-present has_api_key would fully serve the stated 'check settings' purpose. That credential then flows into the MCP client / LLM context (transcripts, logs, possibly a third-party model) with no authorization check of any kind, and is the same Token header used to authenticate every other write-capable tool in this server, so its disclosure is a genuine confidentiality/authorization failure (also fits CWE-522/CWE-306).
contract: Check the current environment settings for DolphinScheduler API

sink: Overwrites the process-wide Config singleton's api_url, which client.py then uses as the base URL (via string concatenation, url = f"{config.api_url}/{path}") for every subsequent tool call in the same running server, including attaching the 'Token' auth header when an api_key is configured
why: api_url is a plain caller-supplied string per this tool's own schema, with no validation, allow-list, or confirmation step, and is stored process-wide (also into the OS environment) so it silently redirects all later tool calls -- and their Authorization/Token header carrying the real DolphinScheduler API key -- to any attacker-chosen host. A caller (or a prompt-injected agent that is induced to call this one tool) can therefore both exfiltrate the configured API credential and have every subsequent create/update/delete call silently routed to a rogue server instead of the real DolphinScheduler instance. Every hop (schema -> Config().api_url setter -> client.request()'s URL/header construction) was read and there is no guard anywhere in the chain.
contract: 更新DolphinScheduler API连接设置 (update DolphinScheduler API connection settings)
